title: Formal glueing of a module map with I-power torsion kernel and cokernel
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. An $R$-module $T$ is *$I$-power torsion* if every $x\in T$ is killed by some power $I^e$; an $S$-module is $I$-power torsion if it is so as an $R$-module. For an $R$-module $P$ write $P\otimes_RS$ for the base change [def-weil-module-base-change] and $u\otimes_RS$ for the base change of an $R$-linear map $u$. (1) Given an $R$-module $N$, an $S$-module $M'$ and an $S$-linear map $\varphi':M'\to N\otimes_RS$ whose kernel and cokernel are $I$-power torsion, there exist an $R$-module $M$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:M'\to M\otimes_RS$ with $(\psi\otimes_RS)\circ\beta=\varphi'$. (2) Given an $R$-module $M$, an $S$-module $N'$ and an $S$-linear map $\varphi':M\otimes_RS\to N'$ whose kernel and cokernel are $I$-power torsion, there exist an $R$-module $N$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:N\otimes_RS\to N'$ with $\beta\circ(\psi\otimes_RS)=\varphi'$. (3) In both cases $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion, and the canonical maps $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$, $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\to\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ induced by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are isomorphisms of $R$-modules; hence, via $\beta$, $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (lemma-application-formal-glueing, line 24882) and its proof (via Proposition 05ER, proposition-equivalence, and Remark 05EL, remark-glueing-data); the final statement (3) via Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301) and Lemma 05E9 (lemma-neighbourhood-isomorphism, line 24264)

proof.text: (Localizing a map with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel.) As $I$ is finitely generated, write $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. Let $T$ be an $I$-power torsion $R$-module and $f=f_i$. For $x\in T$ pick $n\ge1$ with $I^nx=0$; then $f^nx=0$ since $f^n\in I^n$, so $x/1=0$ in $T_f$ and every element $x/f^e=(1/f^e)\cdot(x/1)$ of $T_f$ is $0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]: $T_f=0$. Now let $h:P\to Q$ be an $R$-linear map with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel. Localizing the exact sequences $0\to\operatorname{Ker}h\to P\xrightarrow{h}Q$ and $P\xrightarrow{h}Q\to\operatorname{Coker}h\to0$ at $f$ gives exact sequences $(\operatorname{Ker}h)_f\to P_f\xrightarrow{h_f}Q_f$ and $P_f\xrightarrow{h_f}Q_f\to(\operatorname{Coker}h)_f$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] whose outer terms are $0$; so $h_f$ is injective and surjective, an isomorphism. If $h$ is $S$-linear between $S$-modules, $h_f$ is $S$-linear, because the $S$-action on $P_f$, $Q_f$ is by the localized multiplications and $h_f\circ(s\cdot)_f=(h\circ s\cdot)_f=(s\cdot\circ h)_f=(s\cdot)_f\circ h_f$. In particular, in (1) and (2), $\varphi'_{f_i}$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism for every $i$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0ALK (lemma-application-formal-glueing, line 24882): 'It is clear that the localization varphi_{f_i} is an isomorphism'; Algebra, Proposition 00CS (localization is exact)

proof.text: (Part (1): the glueing datum.) Use the category $\mathrm{Glue}=\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ and the canonical maps $c^P_f$, $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], and the functor $\mathrm{Can}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (1): $\mathrm{Can}(N)=(N\otimes_RS,(N_{f_i}),(c^N_{f_i}),(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}))$ is an object. Put $\mathbf D=(M',(N_{f_i})_i,(\alpha_i)_i,(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$ with $\alpha_i=c^N_{f_i}\circ\varphi'_{f_i}:M'_{f_i}\to N_{f_i}\otimes_RS$, an $S$-linear isomorphism by step 1 and (1) of the proposition. $\mathbf D$ is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$: condition (b) involves only the $N_{f_i}$ and $\sigma^N$, and is condition (b) for $\mathrm{Can}(N)$. For (a): localizing the identity $\sigma^{N\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=(\varphi'_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}$ (both send $(m/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ to $(\varphi'(m)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]) and $(c\circ\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=(c)_{f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}$ (localization is compatible with composition), we get $(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\otimes S)\circ c^{N_{f_i}}_{f_j}\circ(\alpha_i)_{f_j}=(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\otimes S)\circ c^{N_{f_i}}_{f_j}\circ(c^N_{f_i})_{f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=c^{N_{f_j}}_{f_i}\circ(c^N_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{N\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=c^{N_{f_j}}_{f_i}\circ(\alpha_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}$, using (a) for $\mathrm{Can}(N)$ in the middle. Moreover $\Phi=(\varphi',(\mathrm{id}_{N_{f_i}})_i):\mathbf D\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ is a morphism of $\mathrm{Glue}$: $c^N_{f_i}\circ\varphi'_{f_i}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes_RS)\circ\alpha_i$ by definition of $\alpha_i$, and $\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\circ\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0ALK, part (1): the object (M', N_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}, can_ij) of Glue (Remark 05EL, remark-glueing-data) and the morphism to (N tensor S, N_{f_i}, can_i, can_ij) which uses varphi in the first component

proof.text: (Part (1): conclusion.) By [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (2) (essential surjectivity; its hypotheses are those of the lemma with $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$) there are an $R$-module $M$ and an isomorphism $\Theta=(\theta',(\theta_i)_i):\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathbf D$ in $\mathrm{Glue}$; since composition is componentwise [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], $\theta':M\otimes_RS\to M'$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism and each $\theta_i:M_{f_i}\to N_{f_i}$ an isomorphism. The composite $\Phi\circ\Theta:\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ (step 2) is, by full faithfulness in (2), equal to $\mathrm{Can}(\psi)=(\psi\otimes_RS,(\psi_{f_i})_i)$ for a (unique) $R$-linear $\psi:M\to N$. Comparing components: $\psi\otimes_RS=\varphi'\circ\theta'$ and $\psi_{f_i}=\theta_i$. Put $\beta=\theta'^{-1}:M'\to M\otimes_RS$; then $(\psi\otimes_RS)\circ\beta=\varphi'$, which is (1). Record also: $\psi_{f_i}$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0ALK, part (1): 'By Proposition 05ER we conclude that there exists an R-module M such that M' = M tensor S ... This corresponds to an R-module map psi : M -> N (by the equivalence of categories of Proposition 05ER)'

proof.text: (Part (2), the dual argument.) Now $\varphi':M\otimes_RS\to N'$ and by step 1 $\varphi'_{f_i}$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism. Put $\mathbf D'=(N',(M_{f_i})_i,(c^M_{f_i}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})^{-1})_i,(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$. It is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: (b) is (b) for $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (1); for (a), the identity $\sigma^{N'}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=(\varphi'_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}$ (checked on $(m/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]) and $((\varphi'_{f_i})^{-1})_{f_j}=((\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j})^{-1}$ give $\sigma^{M\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}\circ((\varphi'_{f_i})^{-1})_{f_j}=((\varphi'_{f_j})^{-1})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{N'}_{f_i,f_j}$, and (a) for $\mathbf D'$ follows from (a) for $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ exactly as in step 2. $\Phi'=(\varphi',(\mathrm{id}_{M_{f_i}})_i):\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathbf D'$ is a morphism, since $(c^M_{f_i}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})^{-1})\circ\varphi'_{f_i}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes_RS)\circ c^M_{f_i}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (2) there are an $R$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $\Theta=(\theta',(\theta_i)):\mathrm{Can}(N)\to\mathbf D'$, and $\Theta^{-1}\circ\Phi'=\mathrm{Can}(\psi)$ for a unique $R$-linear $\psi:M\to N$; componentwise $\psi\otimes_RS=\theta'^{-1}\circ\varphi'$ and $\psi_{f_i}=\theta_i^{-1}$. Put $\beta=\theta':N\otimes_RS\to N'$, an $S$-linear isomorphism with $\beta\circ(\psi\otimes_RS)=\varphi'$, which is (2); again every $\psi_{f_i}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0ALK, part (2): the object (N', M_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}^{-1}, can_ij) and the morphism from (M tensor S, M_{f_i}, can_i, can_ij), with Proposition 05ER

proof.text: (Part (3): $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion.) In both cases $\psi:M\to N$ has $\psi_{f_i}$ an isomorphism for all $i$ (steps 3, 4). Let $K=\operatorname{Ker}\psi$, $Q=\operatorname{Coker}\psi$. Localizing $0\to K\to M\xrightarrow{\psi}N$ and $M\xrightarrow{\psi}N\to Q\to0$ at $f_i$ gives exact sequences $0\to K_{f_i}\to M_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\psi_{f_i}}N_{f_i}$ and $M_{f_i}\xrightarrow{\psi_{f_i}}N_{f_i}\to Q_{f_i}\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] (applied at each spot); as $\psi_{f_i}$ is injective and surjective, $K_{f_i}=0$ and $Q_{f_i}=0$. Let $x\in K$ (or $x\in Q$). As $x/1=0$ in $K_{f_i}$ there is $e_i\ge1$ with $f_i^{e_i}x=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Put $e=e_1+\dots+e_t$. The ideal $I^e$ is generated by the monomials $f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_t^{a_t}$ with $a_1+\dots+a_t=e$, and each has some $a_i\ge e_i$ (otherwise $\sum a_i\le\sum(e_i-1)<e$), hence kills $x$. So $I^ex=0$: $K$ and $Q$ are $I$-power torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 0ALK, last sentence ('The final statement follows for example from Lemma 05EC'); written out here through the localizations psi_{f_i}, which the construction makes isomorphisms

proof.text: (Part (3): comparison with $\psi\otimes_RS$.) Since $\varphi$ is flat, tensoring the exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{\iota}M\xrightarrow{\psi}N$ with $S$ gives an exact sequence $0\to K\otimes_RS\to M\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\psi\otimes S}N\otimes_RS$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], so $\iota\otimes S:K\otimes_RS\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ is an isomorphism. Tensoring $M\xrightarrow{\psi}N\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\to0$ gives the exact $M\otimes_RS\to N\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\pi\otimes S}Q\otimes_RS\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], so $\pi\otimes S$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes_RS)\to Q\otimes_RS$, $[n\otimes s]\mapsto\pi(n)\otimes s$. As $K$ and $Q$ are $I$-power torsion (step 5) and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, $K\to K\otimes_RS$ and $Q\to Q\otimes_RS$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso]. The composite $K\to K\otimes_RS\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and the composite of $Q\to Q\otimes_RS$ with the inverse of $\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes S)\to Q\otimes_RS$ is $\pi(n)\mapsto[n\otimes1]$ [def-weil-module-base-change]; both are therefore isomorphisms of $R$-modules, which are the canonical maps of (3).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05E9 (lemma-neighbourhood-isomorphism, line 24264) (2) => (1), with flatness of R -> S; Algebra, Lemma 00DF (right exactness of tensor) and Lemma 00HD (flatness)

proof.text: (Part (3): via $\beta$.) In case (1), $\varphi'=(\psi\otimes_RS)\circ\beta$ with $\beta$ an isomorphism, so $\beta$ restricts to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'\to\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'=\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ (same image); in case (2), $\varphi'=\beta\circ(\psi\otimes_RS)$, so $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'=\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_RS)$ and $\beta$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Coker}(\psi\otimes_RS)\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$. With step 6, $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Ker}\varphi'$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Coker}\varphi'$.

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks More on Algebra 0ALK (tags 0ALK, 05ER, 05EL, 05E9, 05E6, 05E7, 05EC checked in tags/tags). Seven steps: localizations phi'_{f_i} are isomorphisms (00CS, existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact); part (1): the glueing datum (M', N_{f_i}, c o phi'_{f_i}, sigma) with its conditions (a),(b) checked from those of Can(N), and the morphism to Can(N); essential surjectivity and full faithfulness of Can give M, beta and psi, with psi_{f_i} isomorphisms; part (2) dually; part (3): Ker psi, Coker psi are I-power torsion because their localizations at the f_i vanish, and K -> K tensor S, Q -> Q tensor S are isomorphisms by 05E9, combined with flat exactness (lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact) and right exactness (lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact). New nodes: def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data (Remark 05EL, with the canonical maps c, sigma made explicit), prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence (05ER: Can is a functor and, under the hypotheses, fully faithful and essentially surjective), lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso (05E9 (2)=>(1)); all unsplit, no Mathlib match. Statement unchanged. The source proves the final statement 'for example from Lemma 05EC'; 05EC alone does not give Ker psi I-power torsion (it needs Ker psi localized at f_i to vanish), so step 5 uses the localizations instead.
